synthesis.prior_interpretation: Earlier negative transfers establish failure for the tested unchanged target alignments after source learning. They do not by themselves reject PorTAL's published freeze-core-and-refit recipe or prove that learned task information is absent.

L1.question: Can target alignment express the learned shared core when calibrated to old generated-adapter functions?
L1.method: Keep learned core and all vectors fixed. Fit target alignment including layer embeddings on10old published tasks; evaluate4heldout old tasks, identity and mismatched-anchor controls. Match scaled DeltaW=(alpha/r)BA rather than arbitrary LoRA factors.
L1.relation_to_primary_work: PorTAL supplies frozen-core target refitting; LoRAGen supplies full-adaptation-matrix supervision. The old-function calibration objective is our hybrid, not the published PorTAL target-task NLL recipe.
L1.behavioral_interpretation: A fresh-input behavioral gain would support recoverable alignment mismatch at this operating point. Geometry recovery without behavior gain would show that old-function calibration is insufficient for the new skills; it would not prove erased information.

L2.question: Does preserving generated adaptations during source learning reduce interference while retaining acquisition and transfer?
L2.method: Matched replay pair with anchor_weight0 versus1,288source updates each. Shared core and current vector learn; source/Qwen4/Mistral alignments and old vectors stay frozen. Published references use initial outputs; prior A/B references use immutable acquisition-boundary outputs.
L2.relation_to_primary_work: Generated-adapter reconstruction supplies a preservation loss. Agent-Dice motivates measuring conflicting updates; Nested Learning motivates richer update organization. This experiment implements neither consensus fusion nor a learned multilevel update rule.
L2.inference_limits: Gains identify the effect of this anchor penalty conditional on replay, these three surfaces and one operating point. They do not identify anchoring-by-replay interaction because no fresh no-replay factorial arms run. Better retention with failed new-task acquisition is not a success.
L2.gates: Both fixed288-update runs finish unless execution is invalid/nonfinite. Own train/validation accuracy>=0.90 and validation gain>=0.50; maximum forgetting from acquisition<=0.05 at every later boundary. Failed source gates stop target evaluation.
L2.execution_boundary: Parent reports anchor0 initial GPU launch failed before any updates because extended target alignment remained on CPU while shared core was on GPU. Parent owns device-only fix and retry. CPU proof did not cover CUDA placement. This is not scientific evidence for or against anchors.

distillation.status: Deferred by parent after frozen free-generation teacher qualification failed.
distillation.rationale: Text-to-LoRA and Doc-to-LoRA show adapter generation/internalization; SDFT and SDPO supply dense teacher signals. These do not remove the need to demonstrate teacher competence under the exact output contract.
distillation.primary_limits: SDFTv2's practical implementation favors forward KL and uses an EMA teacher by default; our proposed fixed competent LoRA teacher would be a distinct hybrid. Doc-to-LoRA reports unrelated-query interference and grows rank under chunk composition.

synthesis.bottom_claim: The justified advance is a testable separation of source acquisition/retention, compatibility with existing target alignments, and behavioral transfer after calibration. None is interchangeable with general continual learning.
